name: Anterior Cutaneous Nerve Entrapment Syndrome
definition: Entrapment of anterior cutaneous thoracoabdominal nerve branches causing focal abdominal-wall neuropathic pain.

investigations.principle: Clinical diagnosis after visceral disease is excluded; diagnostic local anesthetic injection may support localization.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, postoperative, infection, occult injury or condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific pathway.

amber: Persistent symptoms may need pain or surgical nerve evaluation.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Udara/Parshva Vata-neuralgic phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Entrapment of anterior cutaneous thoracoabdominal nerve branches causing focal abdominal-wall neuropathic pain.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, major trauma, unstable fracture/dislocation, sepsis/infection or other listed red flags.
